subject: Civic Education
competence: Explains the importance of being alert about the situations where accidents and disasters might happen.
lesson: Identifies accidents caused by food and drugs highlights the importance of protection: Bad Habit Audit and Safety Jigsaw Roundtable
unique_learning_outcome: Identifies accidents caused by food and drugs highlights the importance of protection.
Explains the importance of being alert about the situations where accidents and disasters might happen.
Explains the importance of safeguarding from accidents other than situational ones by indentifying those situations.

the_entrance: Duration: Exactly 5 minutes. Teacher asks students to share common everyday experiences regarding careless habits, spoiled food, or improper medication use. Students respond with examples from their daily lives. The teacher connects these personal experiences to the day's topic on accident prevention caused by food, drugs, and bad habits, linking directly to the Bad Habit Audit and Safety Jigsaw Roundtable activity.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher organizes the class into 8 teams of 5 students, distributes task cards outlining scenarios on food/drug safety and bad habits, and explains the roles: Leader/Facilitator, Scribe/Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson/Presenter, and Civic Investigator/Inquirer.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students organize into their 8 teams, assign their specific roles, inspect the task cards, and begin analyzing the assigned scenarios involving non-situational accidents caused by negligence.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher monitors room noise and time pacing, prompting teams to classify bad habits versus protective habits and formulate community prevention steps for food and drug related accidents.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Team members actively execute their roles: the Leader keeps focus, the Scribe records arguments, the Timekeeper monitors the 30-minute pacing, the Civic Investigator checks facts against textbook content, and all members collaborate to build a classified list of hazards and protective measures.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher coordinates the presentation sequence, inviting spokespersons to share their group resolutions and facilitating cross-review peer feedback.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Spokespersons present their group's findings and prevention pledges to the class. Other groups evaluate the presentations, ask questions, and offer constructive peer feedback on safety measures.

summary: Consolidation of key concepts emphasizing that man-made accidents—particularly those involving food, drugs, and daily bad habits—can be significantly minimized or avoided through heightened awareness, responsible behavior, and proactive safety measures.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative assessment based on active group participation, accuracy of the bad habit audit classifications, effectiveness of peer feedback during presentations, and individual engagement in assigned roles.
post_activity: Duration: Exactly 5 minutes. In-class concluding task: Each student writes down one personal bad habit they will eliminate and one preventive measure they will adopt regarding food or drug safety in their student notebooks, handing them to the teacher as an exit ticket.
attachments: Task cards detailing scenarios on food
selected_activity:
Activity: Bad Habit Audit and Safety Jigsaw Roundtable
Approach: Student groups examine how daily bad habits and unmonitored situations trigger disasters. Through a structured rotation of investigators, teams synthesize arguments on why breaking bad habits is vital for community safety.
Student task: Groups dissect specific scenarios of non-situational accidents caused by negligence. Investigators gather insights on food/drug safety, secretaries record hazard categories, and presenters share final prevention pledges.
Teacher facilitation: The teacher monitors room noise and time limits, guiding students to connect personal habits with disaster prevention, ensuring every role is actively utilized across all 40 students.
Expected output: A classified list of bad habits versus protective habits, featuring practical community prevention steps.
Grouping: 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer
